headline: Mayor Brenda Locke Leads Unanimous Surrey Council Vote Demanding Public Inquiry into Metro Vancouver
summary: Surrey City Council unanimously passes Mayor Brenda Locke's motion requesting B.C.'s Inspector of Municipalities launch a formal public inquiry into Metro Vancouver financial oversight and regional cost allocations.
body:
SURREY, BC — Surrey City Council voted unanimously to pass a motion introduced by Mayor Brenda Locke calling on the British Columbia Ministry of Municipal Affairs and the Inspector of Municipalities to initiate a comprehensive public inquiry into the governance, financial transparency, and capital budgeting of the Metro Vancouver Regional District (MVRD).

## Regional Financial Transparency and Cost-Sharing Disputes

Mayor Locke stated that Surrey taxpayers contribute tens of millions annually toward regional wastewater and infrastructure megaprojects—such as the North Shore Wastewater Treatment Plant—without adequate board proportional representation or timely access to financial audits. The council resolution formally challenges regional development cost charge (DCC) hikes and demands independent forensic oversight of MVRD administrative expenditures.

Mayor Locke emphasized that as B.C.’s fastest-growing city rapidly approaching a population of 700,000, Surrey must receive transparent accounting for every regional tax dollar collected from local residents.

## Inter-Municipal Solidarity and Council Reaction

Mayors from Langley Township and Delta voiced support for Surrey's call for governance accountability, noting that suburban municipalities carry disproportionate financial burdens under the current regional voting structure.

Surrey councillors across all political parties endorsed the motion to ensure municipal infrastructure priorities take precedence.

## Ministerial Review Process

The Ministry of Municipal Affairs acknowledged receipt of the resolution and confirmed that the Inspector of Municipalities will assess the formal request for audit.

headline: Councillor Linda Annis Pushes Light Rail Transit Priority for King George Boulevard Corridor
summary: Surrey First Councillor Linda Annis challenges regional bus rapid transit proposals, championing permanent street-level light rail transit connecting Surrey City Centre, Newton, and South Surrey.
body:
SURREY, BC — Surrey City Councillor Linda Annis (Surrey First) called on TransLink and the Mayors' Council on Regional Transportation to prioritize permanent street-level Light Rail Transit (LRT) along King George Boulevard over temporary Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) configurations.

## Fixed Transit Infrastructure and Transit-Oriented Density

Councillor Annis argued that fixed-rail transit infrastructure provides the long-term capital certainty required to attract private investment, commercial office space, and purpose-built rental housing along the central spine linking City Centre with South Surrey. She noted that relying on bus rapid transit risks congestion bottlenecks as Surrey continues its rapid demographic expansion.

Councillor Annis highlighted that permanent rail transit stimulates higher-density mixed-use development and creates pedestrian-friendly urban streetscapes along King George Boulevard.

## Council Debate and Financing Strategies

Council members discussed federal and provincial transit infrastructure grant timelines, evaluating cost comparisons between surface rail and high-frequency electric bus lanes.

Business Improvement Associations in Newton supported fixed-rail corridors to stimulate neighborhood commercial rejuvenation.

## Next TransLink Mayors' Council Review

The TransLink Investment Plan updates will be presented before the Mayors' Council in the autumn session.

headline: Councillor Doug Elford Tables Motion to Expand Surrey City Council from 9 to 11 Members
summary: Safe Surrey Coalition Councillor Doug Elford introduces governance reform to add two additional city councillors, ensuring proportional civic representation as Surrey approaches 700,000 residents.
body:
SURREY, BC — Surrey City Councillor Doug Elford (Safe Surrey Coalition) introduced a governance motion before Surrey City Council directing staff to examine expanding the size of council from nine members (mayor and eight councillors) to 11 members.

## Electoral Proportionality and Demographic Growth

Councillor Elford pointed out that while Vancouver has 11 members representing approximately 675,000 residents, Surrey’s eight councillors represent a rapidly expanding population exceeding 680,000 across massive geographic areas including Cloverdale, Fleetwood, Guildford, Newton, and South Surrey. Expanding council size would reduce caseloads per councillor and enhance direct constituent representation.

Councillor Elford underscored that Surrey's explosive growth necessitates modernizing democratic structures that have remained unchanged since 1993.

## Council Vote and Reform Debate

Mayor Brenda Locke and Surrey Connect members opposed the expansion, citing municipal operating costs and arguing that council efficiency remains strong with the current roster.

Civic governance experts supported the proposal, pointing to municipal best practices in major metropolitan jurisdictions.

## Governance Review Roadmap

Council expansion remains an active debate heading into the October 2026 municipal election.

headline: Councillors Harry Bains and Mandeep Nagra Back Municipal Health Administrator to Address ER Wait Times
summary: Surrey Councillors Harry Bains and Mandeep Nagra vote to establish a dedicated municipal health advocacy administrator to coordinate with the provincial government on hospital capacity.
body:
SURREY, BC — Surrey City Councillors Harry Bains (Surrey Connect) and Mandeep Nagra (Safe Surrey Coalition) united across party lines to support council measures establishing a dedicated municipal health liaison to address critical overcrowding at Surrey Memorial Hospital.

## Cross-Party Collaboration for Healthcare Delivery

The approved initiative directs city management to appoint a Senior Health Services Coordinator tasked with expediting development approvals for provincial urgent care centres, expanding diagnostic imaging clinics, and lobbying the Ministry of Health for expedited funding for a second hospital acute care tower in Cloverdale.

Councillor Bains emphasized that local government must proactively assist regional healthcare workers, while Councillor Nagra stressed that patient wait times in Surrey emergency wards require urgent intergovernmental focus.

## Medical Community Reaction and Municipal Coordination

The Surrey Memorial Hospital Physician Association welcomed the municipal advocacy liaison, noting that coordinated land-use planning around hospital zones improves emergency vehicle access.

Council directed the newly established liaison office to report back with a strategic healthcare infrastructure master plan within 90 days.

## Implementation Roadmap

Recruitment for the municipal health services coordinator will commence immediately.
